question: Describe in words the function and the output of the following subroutine. SUBROUTINE GCD (I,J,K) IF (I - J) 1,4,2 1 L = J J = I I = L 2L = I-(I/J){_\ast}J IF(L) 3,4,3 3 I = J J = L GO TO 2 4 K = J RETURN END
options: The program finds the greatest common divisor K of two positive integers I and J.
The program calculates the least common multiple of I and J.
The program calculates the arithmetic mean of I and J and stores the result in K.
The program determines if I is a multiple of J and stores the boolean result in K.
The program adds I and J and stores the result in K.
The program finds the least common multiple of I and J and assigns it to K.
The program multiplies I and J and assigns the product to K.
The program subtracts J from I and stores the result in K.
The program generates a random number between I and J and assigns it to K.
The program computes the sum of all integers between I and J and assigns it to K.
model_outputs:
This SUBROUTINE finds the greatest common divisor of the three input values I, J, and K. The greatest common divisor (GCD) of two or more integers is the largest integer that evenly divides each of them.
The algorithm begins by exchanging I and J if necessary so that I is the smaller of the two. Then, it iteratively divides I by J, and assigns the remainder to L. If L is not zero, it further divides L by J and assigns the remainder to L. If L becomes zero, J is the greatest common divisor of I and J.
The algorithm then handles the case where I is not a multiple of J. In this case, it assigns J to K and returns from the subroutine.
If I is a multiple of J, it computes the greatest common divisor of J and the remainder of I divided by J, and updates the values of I and J accordingly.
The process continues until J becomes the greatest common divisor of all three input values. The final value of J is then stored in K. The answer is (A).

question:
Let G = (V, E) be a finite directed acyclic graph with |E| > 0. Which of the following must be true?
I. G has a vertex with no incoming edge.
II. G has a vertex with no outgoing edge.
III. G has an isolated vertex, that is, one with neither an incoming edge nor an outgoing edge.
options: I and III only
None of the above
I and II only
II and III only
I, II, and a vertex with one outgoing edge
I, II, and a vertex with one incoming edge
All of the above (I, II, III)
II only
I only
III only
model_outputs: An acyclic graph has no cycles. In a cycle, there must be at least one vertex with both incoming and outgoing edges. Thus, in an acyclic graph, every vertex must have either no incoming edge or no outgoing edge. Therefore, both I and II are true. Since every vertex must have either an incoming edge or an outgoing edge, a vertex with neither an incoming edge nor an outgoing edge cannot exist in a directed acyclic graph. The answer is (G).
